text: The system shall allow a visitor to register as a farmer or buyer
Registration shall require a unique email address, password, full name, contact number, role, and basic location
The system shall validate all registration fields on the server
The system shall store passwords using PHP's supported password hashing functions
The system shall allow registered users to log in using email and password
The system shall regenerate the session identifier after successful login
The system shall allow an authenticated user to log out and invalidate the active session
The system shall enforce role-based access for farmer, buyer, and administrator pages and actions
The system shall prevent public registration as an administrator
The system shall deny suspended accounts access to protected functions
An authenticated user shall be able to change the account password after providing the current password
An administrator shall be able to issue a temporary password for a user account without viewing the previous password
A user who receives a temporary password shall be required to change it at the next login
The initial administrator account shall be created by a documented installation or database-seeding procedure and shall require a password change at first login
An authenticated session shall expire after a configured period of inactivity
Passwords shall contain at least 12 characters
Temporary passwords shall expire 24 hours after issuance if unused
Authenticated sessions shall expire after 30 minutes of inactivity
After five failed login attempts for the same normalized email and source IP address within 15 minutes, the system shall block further attempts for that pair for 15 minutes and record the event
A temporary password shall be generated by the system, displayed to the administrator once for secure out-of-band delivery after identity verification, and stored only as a password hash
Issuing a temporary password shall invalidate any previous temporary password and all existing sessions for that account
Farmers and buyers shall be able to view and update their own profile
A profile shall include name, contact number, barangay, municipality or city, and province
A buyer may optionally provide a business name and buyer type
A farmer shall provide farm name, farm description, and a request for administrator verification
A newly registered farmer shall have a pending verification status
A pending or rejected farmer shall not publish produce listings
An administrator shall be able to approve or reject a farmer verification request and record a reason
A farmer shall be able to view the current verification status and rejection reason, when applicable
The system shall not display exact private addresses on public listing pages
Farmer evidence shall be checked offline or through an external process; the first release shall not upload or store identity-document images
The system shall store verification workflow metadata and history but shall not store copies of identity or farm-evidence documents
Verification status shall be pending, approved, rejected, or revoked
Each verification submission shall create an immutable request record with its submission timestamp; a farmer shall have at most one pending request
Each approval, rejection, or revocation shall create an immutable review event containing the decision, reason, reviewer, and review timestamp
A rejected or revoked farmer may update the profile and create a new verification request; previous requests and review events shall remain unchanged
The farmer's current verification status shall be derived from the latest request and review event
An administrator may revoke approval with a required reason; revocation shall follow the same listing and order effects as farmer suspension
An administrator shall be able to create, update, activate, and deactivate produce categories
A category shall have a unique name and optional description
Deactivated categories shall remain associated with historical records but shall not be selectable for new listings
A verified farmer shall be able to create a produce listing
A listing shall include category, produce name, description, available quantity, unit, price per unit, harvest or availability date, barangay, municipality or city, province, and status
A listing may include one validated JPEG, PNG, or WebP produce image no larger than 5 MB
Allowed units shall come from a controlled list such as kilogram, sack, crate, bundle, or piece
A new listing shall have a positive available quantity and price; subsequent quantity adjustments may set available quantity to zero but never below zero
A farmer shall be able to view, edit, close, or reactivate an owned listing subject to the explicit lifecycle rules below
A farmer shall not edit another farmer's listing
The system shall mark a listing unavailable when its available quantity reaches zero
Closed, unavailable, and deactivated listings shall remain available in authorized history views
An administrator shall be able to deactivate a listing that violates system rules and record a reason
Editing a listing shall not change immutable values already stored in an existing order
A farmer may adjust only the current available quantity; quantities already deducted for confirmed or in-progress orders shall not be counted as available stock
Closing a listing shall prevent new order requests but shall not automatically cancel existing pending, delivery-fee-review, confirmed, or in-progress orders
Farmer reactivation shall be allowed only for a farmer-closed listing owned by an active, verified farmer with active category and unit and available quantity greater than zero

An administrator-deactivated listing shall not be reactivated by the farmer; pending and delivery-fee-review requests shall be cancelled, while confirmed or in-progress orders shall be placed under administrative hold
An administrator shall manage the active quantity units available to farmers
Kilograms shall allow quantities with up to two decimal places; sacks, crates, bundles, and pieces shall require whole-number quantities
Deactivating a unit shall prevent its use on new listings without changing historical listings or order snapshots
The system shall decode and re-encode an accepted image into a non-executable generated file and create a display-sized version; the original upload shall not be retained
Listing status shall be exactly one of `active`, `farmer_closed`, `unavailable`, or `admin_deactivated`
A verified, active farmer may create a listing as active when its category and unit are active and available quantity is greater than zero
A farmer may move an owned active or unavailable listing to farmer-closed; no new requests are accepted while it is closed
Every listing status change shall enforce the defined transition and authorization rules on the server and record the actor, timestamp, and required reason

The system shall move an active listing to unavailable when available quantity becomes zero and shall return it to active when quantity becomes positive, unless it was farmer-closed or administrator-deactivated or no longer meets activation conditions

An administrator may move any non-deactivated listing to administrator-deactivated with a reason; only an administrator may restore it, and restoration shall place it in farmer-closed status for farmer review

Deactivating a category or unit shall prevent its use for new listings and prevent affected closed listings from reactivating, but shall not hide an existing active listing or alter historical records
Listing quantity and status changes shall be transactional and shall reject a stale concurrent update rather than overwrite a newer quantity
Each managed unit shall define a quantity precision of zero or two decimal places; kilogram shall be seeded with precision two and sacks, crates, bundles, and pieces with precision zero

Every change to available quantity shall create an immutable stock-adjustment record containing the listing, before quantity, signed change, after quantity, reason category, source type and identifier when applicable, responsible actor, and timestamp

Stock-adjustment reason categories shall include initial listing quantity, farmer correction, order confirmation, pre-preparation cancellation, and administrator restoration; the recorded before quantity plus signed change shall equal after quantity
Restoration exposure shall equal the requested quantities of the listing's confirmed and in-progress orders because those quantities may still be restored by cancellation

A farmer stock increase shall be rejected when available quantity plus restoration exposure would exceed `999,999.99`; order confirmation transfers quantity from available quantity into restoration exposure, while completion or administrator non-restoration removes that exposure

A listing whose expiry date has passed shall be presented as expired and shall be rejected both when an order is requested and when a pending order is confirmed; it shall remain visible in the catalogue rather than being silently removed, so that the rejection is observable rather than invisible

Expiry shall not alter a listing's recorded available quantity, because the stock still exists and an expired listing is withheld from sale rather than written off; expiry shall therefore never produce a stock adjustment
Visitors and authenticated users shall be able to browse active listings
Users shall be able to search by produce name or farmer or farm name
Users shall be able to filter by category, location, unit, availability date, and price range
Users shall be able to sort by newest listing, lowest price, highest price, and nearest availability date
Search and filter results shall use pagination
Public results shall not reveal private contact details or exact addresses
Only an authenticated buyer with an active account shall be able to submit an order request
An order request shall reference one active produce listing and one buyer
A buyer shall provide requested quantity, fulfillment method, preferred fulfillment date, and optional notes
Fulfillment method shall be pickup or farmer-arranged local delivery
A local-delivery request shall require a delivery address appropriate for coordination
The system shall calculate the order subtotal from requested quantity and the listing price at the time of order
The system shall preserve the agreed unit price in the order even if the listing price changes later
Submitting an order shall create a pending request and shall not immediately deduct listing quantity
A farmer shall be able to accept a pickup request, quote a delivery fee for a local-delivery request, or reject a pending request for an owned listing
Confirming an order shall deduct its requested quantity from available quantity using a database transaction
The system shall prevent confirmation when the requested quantity exceeds the listing's available quantity
Rejecting an order shall require a reason and shall not change listing quantity
The farmer shall be able to move a confirmed order through valid preparation and fulfillment statuses
The buyer shall be able to view the current status and status history of an owned order
The farmer shall be able to view incoming and historical orders for owned listings

For a pending local-delivery request, the listing owner and administrators may view the delivery address needed to assess service and quote a fee; direct contact details remain hidden until confirmation
The system shall not record or process online payment information
Each order shall preserve immutable snapshots of produce name, unit, requested quantity, unit price, subtotal, fulfillment method, and the fulfillment location details agreed at confirmation
For farmer-arranged local delivery, the farmer shall enter a non-negative delivery-fee quote, including zero when delivery is free, before the buyer confirms the order
The system shall calculate and store the produce subtotal, delivery fee, and final total; pickup orders shall have a delivery fee of zero
Delivery fees and final totals are records for coordination only and shall not constitute online payment processing
A farmer accepting a pickup request shall provide the private pickup location and confirm the order atomically with stock deduction
Quoting a local-delivery fee shall move the request to delivery-fee review without deducting stock
A buyer shall be able to accept or decline the quoted delivery fee; acceptance shall confirm the order and deduct stock atomically, while decline shall cancel it without changing stock
If stock is insufficient when the buyer accepts a delivery quote, the system shall cancel the request as unavailable without changing stock
After confirmation, the buyer and farmer shall be able to view each other's coordination contact details and the applicable private delivery or pickup location

Once a request enters delivery-fee review, its quantity, unit price, fulfillment method, delivery address, and quoted fee shall be immutable; either party must cancel or reject it before a changed request can be submitted
The system shall reject a new request whose quantity exceeds the listing's available quantity at submission time, while making clear that pending requests do not reserve stock
Order snapshots shall also preserve the category name, farmer or farm display name, and listing location as they existed when the request was submitted
A pickup order may follow `pending -> confirmed -> preparing -> ready_for_pickup -> completed`
A local-delivery order may follow `pending -> delivery_fee_review -> confirmed -> preparing -> out_for_delivery -> completed`
A farmer may move a pending request to rejected and may withdraw a delivery quote by moving a request in delivery-fee review to rejected; a reason is required
A buyer may cancel a pending request or decline and cancel a request in delivery-fee review
A buyer or farmer may cancel a confirmed order before it enters preparing status; a reason is required
Every status change shall record the previous status, new status, responsible actor (user or system), timestamp, and optional note
The system shall reject invalid status transitions
Cancelling a confirmed order before preparing shall restore its requested quantity to available quantity in the same database transaction as the cancellation

After an order enters preparing, only an administrator may cancel it as part of dispute or suspension resolution; the administrator shall record a reason and a stock disposition of restored or not restored
Rejected, completed, and cancelled orders are terminal and shall not move to another status
An administrative hold is separate from the primary order status; while held, no buyer or farmer status transition is allowed
An administrator may release a held order without changing its primary status only after involved accounts are active and any administrator-deactivated listing has been restored
An administrator may cancel a held confirmed or in-progress order and must record whether stock was restored or not restored, with a reason for that stock disposition

Rejection and cancellation shall record a controlled reason category: buyer changed mind, farmer unavailable, stock unavailable, fulfillment unavailable, administrator action, dispute, or other; an explanatory note is required for other, administrator action, and dispute

An administrator may cancel an abandoned pending request with no transition for seven days or delivery-fee-review request with no transition for 48 hours, using the administrator-action reason category and an explanatory note; this transition shall not change available quantity
The administrator dashboard shall display counts of users, pending farmer verifications, active listings, pending orders, and completed orders
An administrator shall be able to search and filter users by name, role, status, and registration date
An administrator shall be able to activate or suspend a user account and record a reason
Suspending an account shall invalidate its active sessions and preserve historical records
An administrator shall be able to view listings and orders for oversight
An administrator shall not change ownership of a listing or order
Sensitive administrator actions shall be written to an audit log
Suspending or revoking a farmer shall move all active or unavailable listings to administrator-deactivated and cancel pending or delivery-fee-review requests without changing stock
Confirmed and in-progress orders involving a suspended user or administrator-deactivated listing shall remain visible to the parties and administrator under an administrative hold
Suspending a buyer shall cancel that buyer's pending and delivery-fee-review requests without changing stock and place confirmed and in-progress orders under administrative hold
An administrator shall be able to create, rename, activate, and deactivate quantity units, subject to historical-record preservation rules
An active administrator shall be able to create another administrator account with a temporary password and forced password change; public administrator registration remains prohibited
The system shall prevent an administrator from suspending the same account and shall prevent suspension of the last active administrator
An administrator shall resolve each held order by either releasing the hold under FR-STAT-012 or cancelling it under FR-STAT-013
An audit event shall record event type, acting user, target type and identifier, timestamp, outcome, source IP address, request identifier, reason when required, and relevant before-and-after values

Audited events shall include authentication administration, administrator-account creation, user activation or suspension, verification decisions, category and unit changes, listing deactivation or restoration, order holds and resolutions, retention holds, and report generation
Audit events shall be append-only through application functions and shall not be editable or deletable by ordinary administrator actions
An administrator shall be able to place and release a retention hold on specified records with a reason and timestamp; both actions shall be audited
Retention processing shall skip records under an active hold and shall anonymize an eligible account only when it has no nonterminal orders and all related retention periods have expired
When creating a unit, the administrator shall select whether it accepts whole numbers or up to two decimal places; precision cannot be changed after the unit has been used by a listing
An administrator shall be able to generate a user registration report filtered by date and role
An administrator shall be able to generate a listing report filtered by date, category, farmer, and status
An administrator shall be able to generate an order report filtered by date, status, farmer, and buyer
A farmer shall be able to view a summary of listing quantities and orders by status
Reports shall display the applied filters and generation timestamp
The first release shall support printable HTML reports. PDF export is optional only if time remains
An administrator shall be able to generate a farmer-verification report filtered by submission date, review date, status, and reviewer

An administrator shall be able to generate a fulfillment-value report showing order counts, produce subtotals, delivery fees, and final totals filtered by date, fulfillment method, farmer, and order status
An administrator shall be able to generate a cancellation summary grouped and filtered by date, cancelling role, order stage, farmer, buyer, and recorded reason
Validation failures shall reject the operation without partial database changes and shall return field-specific messages without exposing sensitive internals
Historical snapshots shall retain previously valid values even when current validation rules, categories, or units later change
Monetary calculations shall use fixed-point decimal arithmetic and round to two decimal places only at the line-total calculation boundary
Email, category name, and unit name uniqueness checks shall be case-insensitive after normalization
Decoded listing images shall not exceed 20 megapixels or 6,000 pixels on either side, and generated display images shall have a maximum longest side of 1,600 pixels

Before accepting a request or delivery quote, the system shall reject any operation whose calculated subtotal or final total would exceed `9,999,999.99`; no accepted multiplication or addition may exceed the monetary storage bound
All SQL queries containing variable data shall use PDO prepared statements
All state-changing forms shall include CSRF protection
All untrusted output shall be HTML-escaped by default
Passwords shall use `password_hash()` and `password_verify()`
Production session cookies shall set HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Lax
The session identifier shall be regenerated after login and privilege changes
Authorization shall be enforced on the server for every protected action
Login attempts shall enforce the five-attempt, 15-minute window and 15-minute block defined in FR-AUTH-019 without revealing whether an email is registered
Uploaded images shall be checked by content type, extension, decoded image validity, and the 5 MB file-size limit; generated filenames shall be used
Uploaded images shall be stored in a dedicated location where script execution is disabled; only generated filenames and image extensions shall be served
Production error pages shall not expose stack traces, SQL statements, credentials, or server paths
Sensitive administrator actions and order status changes shall be auditable
Any non-local production deployment shall use HTTPS for every application request and redirect HTTP requests to HTTPS
Production responses shall set HSTS, Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, frame-embedding protection, and a strict Referrer-Policy
Temporary passwords, reset events, retention holds, and administrative hold resolutions shall follow the same hashing, authorization, CSRF, and audit controls as other sensitive actions
PHP strict session mode shall be enabled, and uninitialized client-supplied session identifiers shall be rejected

Production HSTS shall use a max-age of at least 31,536,000 seconds; CSP shall restrict default, script, and style sources to self and set `object-src 'none'`, `base-uri 'self'`, and `frame-ancestors 'none'`; Referrer-Policy shall be `no-referrer`; and X-Content-Type-Options shall be `nosniff`
Temporary passwords and authentication secrets shall never be written to application logs or audit before-and-after values
Audit before-and-after payloads shall use an allowlist of non-sensitive fields and shall not copy passwords, tokens, contact details, exact addresses, free-text notes, or uploaded content
The system shall collect only information required for account, verification, listing, and order coordination
Public pages shall not display private phone numbers, email addresses, or exact addresses
Users shall be informed why profile and fulfillment information is collected
Access to personal data shall follow role and ownership rules consistent with the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (RA 10173)
Historical orders, status changes, verification reviews, suspension records, and audit logs shall follow the five-year retention and anonymization rules in BR-033 and BR-034

Account anonymization shall replace the user's name, email, contact number, exact addresses, farm or business name, and free-text profile fields with non-identifying values while preserving a stable internal subject reference, non-identifying order values, statuses, dates, and required audit relationships
Only active administrators may create or release retention holds, and each hold shall identify its scope, reason, creator, creation time, status, release actor, and release time
Before a buyer submits a local-delivery request, the interface shall disclose that the exact delivery address will be visible to the listing owner for service assessment before confirmation
Anonymization shall also remove exact fulfillment locations and user-authored free-text that contains personal data while preserving non-identifying reason categories and aggregate values

Audit events shall identify actors and targets by stable internal references; personal values shall remain only in their authoritative records where retention and anonymization controls can be applied
At least 95% of common page requests shall complete within 3 seconds during the defined 20-concurrent-user acceptance test on the documented target environment
Listing and administrative tables shall use pagination
Searchable and relational columns shall be indexed according to measured query needs
Uploaded listing images shall be re-encoded and served from a display-sized generated version rather than the original upload

The acceptance-test report shall identify server hardware, PHP and MySQL versions, database size, network conditions, tested routes, request mix, and measured percentile results; common requests are login, listing browse/search/detail, order submission/detail, and administrator dashboard/report views
The interface shall be responsive from 320-pixel mobile screens through common desktop widths
Primary interactive controls shall be keyboard accessible
Form fields shall have visible labels, validation messages, and clear recovery instructions
Text and interactive controls shall meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast requirements
Status shall not be communicated by color alone
Navigation and terminology shall remain consistent across roles
The system shall provide useful empty, success, warning, and error states
Foreign keys and database constraints shall protect required relationships
Order confirmation and stock deduction shall run in one database transaction
The deployment shall support daily database backups with a maximum recovery point of 24 hours, a target restore time of 4 hours, and a documented successful restore test before release
User-facing records shall use status changes or soft deletion instead of destructive deletion where history is required
The application shall show a safe error message and preserve submitted values when a recoverable form error occurs
Application code shall separate configuration, database access, business logic, controllers or actions, and views
Reusable validation, authorization, CSRF, session, and escaping functions shall be centralized
Names shall describe business meaning and follow one documented convention
Environment-specific database credentials shall not be committed to version control
The project shall include installation, database setup, and test instructions
Acceptance testing shall cover the current stable releases of Chrome, Edge, and Firefox available at the time of release
Responsive acceptance testing shall include 360-pixel mobile, 768-pixel tablet, and 1366-pixel desktop viewport widths
The load test shall simulate 20 concurrent users performing a documented representative mix of browsing, searching, authentication, order submission, and administration actions

Security tests shall cover horizontal and vertical authorization, CSRF, stored and reflected XSS, SQL injection, malicious uploads, login throttling, session fixation, session expiry, suspension invalidation, and order-confirmation concurrency
Production-header tests shall verify HTTPS redirection, HSTS, Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, frame-embedding protection, Referrer-Policy, and secure cookie attributes
